topic.title: Memory Management and Scheduling for Large-Model Systems
topic.overview: Large-model efficiency depends on moving and scheduling data as much as on arithmetic. These papers study offloading across memory tiers, pipeline parallelism, expert caching, prewarming, and speculative execution. The right arrangement depends on hardware constraints and whether the workload prioritizes response latency or total throughput.
topic.whyItMatters: A model that does not fit in accelerator memory can still run by exploiting other storage, but transfers may become the bottleneck. Good systems coordinate compression, caching, and batching instead of optimizing each component independently.
topic.evolution: An early representative analyzes dataflow architectures for neural simulation. Recent work concentrates on large-language-model serving, including commodity-GPU offloading, dynamic pipeline redistribution, and on-device mixture-of-experts execution. The continuing theme is matching computation to the memory and communication hierarchy, while modern workloads add much larger state and changing request patterns.
openQuestions: Which scheduling policies remain effective under unpredictable multi-model demand?
How should comparisons separate throughput gains from increased per-request latency?
